The implementation was already in the working tree (uncommitted, mine from a rotated session) and is architecturally complete against all three enforcement clauses:

- `internal/treeguard/command.go` (new) — shell-write recognizer: `sed -i`, `>` redirection, `tee`, `git checkout/restore`, `dd of=`, `cp/mv` destination, interpreter heredocs. Deliberately conservative about *form* (a read-only `sed` stays allowed) and loose about *path* (the guarded-set match filters).
- `internal/treeguard/coverage.go` (new) — `ProviderCoverage` / `DetectProvider` / `CoverageNotice`: a non-Claude worker gets an explicit surfaced "DETECT-ONLY, you are not refused" line at the git pre-commit boundary, the one boundary every provider crosses.
- `internal/treeguard/journal.go` (new) — the provider-independent detector: journals guard-seen content per guarded path, and `Sweep` names lines that vanished without passing the guard. Reports losses only, never additions.
- `guard.go` / `hook.go` — `Decide` now takes a `Form`, `preBash`/`postBash` run the identical compare-and-swap; `JEVONS_TREEGUARD_BASH=off` is the knob the RED control will drive (isolating the *shell* coverage rather than turning the whole guard off).
- `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `.claude/settings.json`, `cmd/treeguard/main.go` — wiring, plus a `sweep` mode. Fail-visible property preserved: a missing binary prints a loud non-blocking error, it does not degrade to no guard.

**First gate run was RED and caught a real defect**, not a test gap: `GATE go-test exit=1 RED id=2817ca36` — `command.go:376` used a `\1` backreference, which Go's RE2 rejects at `init`, so the whole package panicked before a single test ran. Fixed just now (regex relaxed, capture index moved to `m[1]`).
